service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: Request date is the reference point. 69-year-old woman with myelodysplastic syndrome (ICD-10-CM D46.9) diagnosed 5 months ago with transfusion-dependent anemia and thrombocytopenia. Bone marrow biopsy 3 weeks ago: 7% blasts with intermediate-risk cytogenetics. Her IPSS-R score, calculated and documented by the hematologist, is 4.5 (high risk). No HLA-matched sibling or unrelated adult donor was found, so an allogeneic transplant using umbilical cord blood stem cell products is planned after reduced-intensity conditioning. Cardiac, pulmonary, renal and hepatic testing show adequate organ function. The transplant center is experienced in cord blood transplantation.
rationale_note: Boundary: IPSS-R exactly 4.5 meets the >= 4.5 threshold; cord blood is an allowed stem cell source.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 66-year-old man with multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00), International Staging System (ISS) Stage II at diagnosis 14 months ago, high-risk cytogenetics, in very good partial response after induction and a prior autologous transplant. An allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant from an HLA-matched unrelated donor is requested. He has signed informed consent and is enrolled in a prospective clinical study of allogeneic HSCT for multiple myeloma that appears on the CMS list of approved Coverage with Evidence Development studies; the study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov, its protocol addresses graft-versus-host disease, transplant-related adverse events and overall survival, and its analysis plan adjusts for age, ISS stage, conditioning regimen, donor type and cell source.
rationale_note: Allogeneic HSCT for ISS stage II myeloma inside a CMS-approved CED study: both C3 and C4 met.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 61-year-old woman with Durie-Salmon Stage III multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) who relapsed 10 months after an autologous transplant and is now in partial response after salvage therapy. An allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant from her HLA-identical brother is requested. Organ function is adequate and she has an excellent performance status. The transplant center does not participate in any clinical study of allogeneic transplant for myeloma; the transplant will be performed as standard care, and she is not enrolled in any study or registry.
rationale_note: Allogeneic HSCT for myeloma is covered only within an approved prospective study; this patient is treated off-study.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 64-year-old man with primary myelofibrosis (ICD-10-CM D47.1) diagnosed 2 years ago, with splenomegaly and constitutional symptoms partly controlled on ruxolitinib. His hematologist documents a DIPSSplus risk category of Intermediate-1. He is enrolled, with signed informed consent, in a CMS-approved prospective clinical study of allogeneic HSCT for myelofibrosis registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. An allogeneic transplant from a matched unrelated donor is requested.
rationale_note: DIPSSplus Intermediate-1 does not meet the Intermediate-2 or High requirement, even inside an approved study.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 67-year-old woman with post-polycythemia vera (secondary) myelofibrosis (ICD-10-CM D47.1) with progressive anemia and a spleen 14 cm below the costal margin. She is enrolled, with signed informed consent, in a CMS-approved prospective clinical study of allogeneic HSCT for myelofibrosis registered on ClinicalTrials.gov. An allogeneic transplant from an HLA-matched sibling is requested. The referral packet contains the bone marrow pathology report and donor typing; no DIPSS, DIPSSplus or other prognostic risk score is recorded anywhere in the record.
rationale_note: Patient is in an approved MF study, but no DIPSSplus risk category is documented, so eligibility cannot be confirmed.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 78-year-old man with biopsy-proven primary (AL) amyloid light chain amyloidosis (ICD-10-CM E85.81) with lambda light chains, with amyloid involvement of the kidneys (nephrotic-range proteinuria) and heart; no liver, nerve or gastrointestinal involvement on evaluation. Echocardiogram 2 weeks ago shows a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%. The team selected him using recognized clinical risk factors (troponin, NT-proBNP, performance status). High-dose melphalan followed by autologous stem cell transplantation is requested.
rationale_note: Primary AL amyloidosis, 2 organs, EF 55%. Age 78 is a distractor: the age >= 64 exclusion applied only through March 14, 2005.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 63-year-old woman with primary (AL) amyloid light chain amyloidosis (ICD-10-CM E85.81) confirmed on fat pad and renal biopsy, with amyloid involvement limited to the kidneys and heart. Recognized clinical risk factors were used to select her for transplant. Echocardiogram 1 week ago reports a left ventricular ejection fraction of 45%; a cardiac MRI the same week also measured 45%. Renal function is moderately reduced and she is fully ambulatory. High-dose melphalan with autologous stem cell transplantation is requested.
rationale_note: Boundary miss: LVEF exactly 45% is not greater than 45%.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 62-year-old man with Durie-Salmon Stage III multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) who received a first autologous stem cell transplant 3 months ago after induction (very good partial response, paraprotein down 92%, sustained). Cardiac, renal, pulmonary and hepatic function are adequate. Per the transplant center's planned protocol, a second autologous stem cell transplant (the second of two planned sequential rounds) is now requested to deepen the response.
rationale_note: Second planned AuSCT for myeloma is tandem transplantation, which is non-covered.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 71-year-old woman with Durie-Salmon Stage III IgG kappa multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) diagnosed 6 months ago. After four cycles of induction chemotherapy her serum M-protein fell from 4.0 to 1.8 g/dL (a 55% decrease), and the reduction has been sustained on repeat testing for 6 weeks. Pre-transplant evaluation documents LVEF 60%, creatinine clearance 65 mL/min, DLCO 78% predicted and normal liver function tests. She has not had a prior transplant. A single autologous stem cell transplant after high-dose melphalan is requested.
rationale_note: Single AuSCT, Durie-Salmon stage III, partial response (55% paraprotein drop sustained 6 weeks), adequate organ function documented.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 68-year-old man with IgA multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) staged as Durie-Salmon Stage I (hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, normal calcium, a single small lytic lesion, low M-protein). He is newly diagnosed and responded to induction chemotherapy with a 70% decrease in serum paraprotein sustained for 2 months. Cardiac, renal, pulmonary and hepatic function are all adequate. A single autologous stem cell transplant is requested.
rationale_note: Durie-Salmon stage I: single AuSCT for myeloma is covered only for stage II or III.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 65-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia (ICD-10-CM C92.00) that is primary refractory: after two induction courses, day-28 bone marrow shows 30% blasts. She has no HLA-matched sibling or unrelated donor. Organ function is adequate. Her physician requests high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplantation using stem cells collected earlier.
rationale_note: AuSCT for acute leukemia not in remission is explicitly non-covered.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 64-year-old man with Durie-Salmon Stage II multiple myeloma (ICD-10-CM C90.00) diagnosed 5 months ago. After induction his urine and serum paraprotein fell by 65%, sustained for 2 months on repeat testing. This would be his first transplant; a single autologous stem cell transplant is requested. The submitted record contains the staging workup, the response labs and the induction treatment notes, but no echocardiogram, pulmonary function testing, renal function or liver function results and no statement about organ function.
rationale_note: Stage II, responsive myeloma, single AuSCT, but no assessment of cardiac, renal, pulmonary or hepatic function is in the record.

service: Stem cell transplantation (allogeneic HSCT or autologous stem cell transplantation)
vignette: 66-year-old man with relapsed metastatic nonseminomatous germ cell tumor of the testis (ICD-10-CM C62.91) that recurred after first-line cisplatin-based chemotherapy. His oncologist requests high-dose chemotherapy with autologous stem cell rescue. Organ function is adequate and stem cells have been collected.
rationale_note: AuSCT for a solid tumor other than neuroblastoma (germ cell tumor) is non-covered.
